name: Galvanic Disruption Gauntlet GDG-2 'Palsy'
description:
The GDG-2 is a form-fitting combat gauntlet extending from fingertip to mid-forearm, constructed from a conductive polymer shell over a flexible titanium mesh substrate. Embedded within the palm and finger surfaces are a series of galvanic discharge nodes capable of delivering precisely modulated electrical pulses on contact. Unlike crude shock weapons, the GDG-2 does not simply stun — its discharge profile is engineered to induce involuntary neuromuscular disruption in specific muscle groups, causing targeted tremor, grip failure, or full limb incapacitation depending on where contact is made and which discharge mode is selected.

The gauntlet interfaces with a compact forearm-mounted controller that allows the operator to toggle between three discharge profiles: a grip-failure mode targeting hand and forearm musculature, a leg-incapacitation mode calibrated for thigh and calf contact, and a full-body seizure mode reserved for maximum-force situations. The system includes a biometric lock keyed to the operator's galvanic skin signature, preventing the gauntlet from discharging if removed from its registered user. The polymer shell is rated for light impact protection and provides partial insulation against return electrical hazards.

The GDG-2 was originally developed for law enforcement crowd management and non-lethal suspect control, but its discharge profiles were quietly expanded in the Mk2 revision to include settings that can induce cardiac arrhythmia on sustained contact. This revision was never publicly documented, and ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC has consistently denied any lethality potential in official materials.
tier_availability: Tier 2+ (law enforcement); Black market (Mk2 full profile)
legality: Licensed (law enforcement issue); Prohibited (civilian Mk2 profile)
specifications:
coverage: Fingertip to mid-forearm
discharge nodes: 14
discharge profiles: 3
peak output: 0.8–4.2 joules (profile-dependent)
power source: Forearm-mounted power cell, 200 full discharges per charge
shell material: Conductive polymer over titanium mesh
biometric lock: Galvanic skin signature recognition
weight: 420g
tactical_use: Law enforcement operators use the GDG-2 to control suspects without drawing firearms in politically sensitive environments. Grip-failure mode is applied during disarming maneuvers. In private security contexts, operators target joint contact points to drop a subject without visible injury, which is valued in corporate settings where discretion matters. Mk2 operators with full profile access use the cardiac mode as a last resort in close-quarters assassination scenarios where silence is paramount.
cultural_context: The GDG-2 is a symbol of institutional authority in GLMZ — seeing an officer wearing one signals you are in a district with resources and governance, for better or worse. Among the underclass, 'getting shook' by a Palsy is a humiliating form of public control that has sparked at least two district-level protests in recent years. On the black market, the Mk2's hidden lethality profile has made it a favorite of corporate cleaners who need deniable methods, and the gauntlet's medical appearance allows it to pass casual inspection.
known_users: Undercover agents requiring concealed force options
Black market 'cleaners' operating in high-profile corporate spaces
story_hooks: A municipal officer dies of apparent cardiac arrest during a routine arrest — witnesses report she was wearing a GDG-2 during the struggle, raising the question of whether the suspect accessed the gauntlet's undocumented lethality profile or whether the device malfunctioned.

A whistleblower from ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC is trying to leak documentation of the Mk2's hidden cardiac mode to a journalist, but they've gone quiet. The last message they sent mentioned someone wearing a Palsy gauntlet had been following them.

A crime lord runs an underground fighting circuit where combatants are required to use GDG-2 gauntlets — the spectacle of watching fighters lose muscular control mid-bout is the main attraction, and the matches are broadcast illegally to wealthy subscribers citywide.
related_entities: Zheng-Dao Heavy Industries Siege Mortar SM-8 'Tremor'

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, predatory combat glove that clings to the hand like a second skin. The GDG-2 has an aggressive, almost organic silhouette—fingertips taper slightly, and subtle ridges run along the knuckles where discharge nodes sit flush against the surface. The forearm section swells slightly at mid-point where the controller housing integrates, creating an asymmetrical profile that reads as purposeful rather than awkward.
physical_description.dimensions: Fingertip to mid-forearm: 35cm total length. Palm width: 8.5cm. Controller housing depth: 2.2cm. Individual discharge node diameter: 0.6cm.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light in hand—420g total feels almost negligible when worn, distributing weight evenly across the forearm. The titanium mesh substrate creates a responsive, almost alive sensation that shifts slightly with hand movement. Heavy enough to feel engineered, light enough to forget you're wearing it until the nodes activate.
physical_description.primary_material: Conductive polymer shell (outer layer) over flexible titanium mesh substrate (structural layer). Forearm controller housing is brushed steel with reinforced polymer panels. Internal conduction pathways use embedded copper-nickel tracery.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal conductive polymer with microscopically textured surface to improve contact conductivity. The titanium mesh visible at stress points (knuckles, finger joints) shows a brushed silver-grey finish with faint anodization marks. Controller housing features worn brushed steel with minor oxidation patina. No chrome or gloss—everything designed for light absorption and professional subtlety.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: Deep charcoal grey (#2B2D31). Accents: Brushed steel grey (#8A8C8E) at mesh points and controller. Subtle emerald LED indicator ring around the controller (when powered, indicates mode selection). Biometric lock plate displays amber when locked, green when authorized.
physical_description.grip_texture: The palm and finger surfaces have a deliberate grip-cone texture—micro-ridges that feel almost organic, designed to maximize surface contact without being visibly aggressive. Not rubberized; more akin to textured silicone. The inside of the gauntlet (against skin) features a softer, slightly tacky polymer that prevents slipping during extended wear. Controller buttons are recessed steel with subtle tactile feedback.
distinctive_features: 14 galvanic discharge nodes distributed across palm and fingers—visible as slightly raised, perfectly circular contact points with micro-etched ZHENG-DAO symbols
Three-stage biometric lock indicator plate on wrist section; transitions amber→green when galvanic signature recognized
Forearm-mounted controller with three deeply recessed mode-selection buttons (unmarked, identified by subtle haptic feedback)
Faint copper tracery visible through translucent sections of polymer shell—shows internal conduction pathways under certain lighting
Micro-ventilation ports along the inner forearm (cooling for extended discharge cycles)
Subtle wear pattern on contact nodes in used units—slight polishing from repeated skin contact during testing/deployment
Battery status indicator: tiny LED beneath controller housing flashes green (charged) or amber (low)
No obvious seams or construction lines—appears almost molded as a single unit
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: ZHENG-DAO BIOELECTRIC logo (stylized DNA helix) stamped on controller housing in small serif characters. Serial plate recessed into wrist section—16-digit alphanumeric identifier. 'GDG-2' designation laser-etched in tiny characters on the inside of the forearm section (only visible to wearer). Law enforcement units have additional regulation stamps; civilian/black market Mk2 units typically have these filed or laser-burned away.
physical_description.condition_typical: Authorized law enforcement units are usually field-maintained, showing minor scuffing on the knuckle nodes and occasional polymer scratches from gear contact. Black market Mk2 units are either pristine (freshly stolen from armory) or heavily modified—field-stripped and repainted, controller swapped with aftermarket variants, or with unlicensed discharge calibration marks. Heavy users show polished contact nodes and slight discoloration around the discharge points from repeated electrical discharge.
